title: Enterprise Architecture Patterns
description: Master advanced PEGA enterprise architecture patterns, design principles, and scalable system design methodologies
learning_objectives: Design scalable enterprise PEGA architectures using proven patterns
Implement microservices and distributed system patterns with PEGA
Establish architectural governance and design standards
Optimize system integration and data flow architectures

content.text: Enterprise PEGA architectures require sophisticated design patterns that handle massive scale, complex integrations, and diverse user requirements while maintaining performance, reliability, and maintainability. Advanced architectural patterns provide blueprints for building robust, scalable systems that can evolve with business needs.

# Enterprise PEGA Architecture Blueprint
enterprise_architecture:
  name: "Scalable-PEGA-Enterprise-Platform"
  
  # Presentation Layer
  presentation_tier:
    web_tier:
      components:
        - name: "pega_portal_servers"
          instances: 4
          load_balancing: "round_robin_with_affinity"
          session_management: "distributed_cache"
        - name: "cdn_edge_servers"
          provider: "cloudflare"
          caching_strategy: "aggressive_static_content"
        - name: "api_gateway"
          type: "enterprise_gateway"
          features: ["rate_limiting", "authentication", "monitoring"]
    
    mobile_tier:
      components:
        - name: "mobile_api_layer"
          optimization: "lightweight_payloads"
          offline_capability: "enabled"
        - name: "push_notification_service"
          provider: "firebase_cloud_messaging"
          delivery_guarantee: "at_least_once"
  
  # Application Layer
  application_tier:
    pega_cluster:
      topology: "active_active_multi_site"
      nodes:
        - site: "primary_datacenter"
          instances: 8
          node_types: ["interactive", "batch", "search"]
          resource_allocation:
            interactive_nodes: 60%
            batch_nodes: 30%
            search_nodes: 10%
        - site: "disaster_recovery_datacenter"
          instances: 4
          node_types: ["interactive", "batch"]
          replication: "real_time_async"
    
    microservices_layer:
      service_mesh: "istio"
      services:
        - name: "customer_service"
          pattern: "domain_driven_design"
          data_consistency: "eventual_consistency"
        - name: "notification_service"
          pattern: "event_driven_architecture"
          message_broker: "apache_kafka"
        - name: "analytics_service"
          pattern: "cqrs_event_sourcing"
          read_models: "elasticsearch"
  
  # Data Layer
  data_tier:
    primary_database:
      type: "postgresql_cluster"
      configuration: "master_slave_with_read_replicas"
      partitioning_strategy: "horizontal_by_tenant"
      backup_strategy: "continuous_wal_archiving"
    
    cache_layer:
      distributed_cache:
        type: "redis_cluster"
        topology: "3_master_3_slave"
        eviction_policy: "lru_with_ttl"
      application_cache:
        type: "hazelcast_grid"
        persistence: "write_through"
    
    data_lake:
      storage: "hdfs_with_s3_backup"
      processing: "apache_spark"
      governance: "apache_atlas"
  
  # Integration Layer
  integration_tier:
    enterprise_service_bus:
      type: "apache_camel_with_pega_connectors"
      message_patterns: ["request_reply", "publish_subscribe", "message_routing"]
      transaction_management: "distributed_xa_transactions"
    
    api_management:
      platform: "kong_enterprise"
      features:
        - oauth2_authentication
        - rate_limiting_per_consumer
        - request_response_transformation
        - analytics_and_monitoring
    
    event_streaming:
      platform: "apache_kafka_cluster"
      topics:
        - name: "case_events"
          partitions: 12
          replication_factor: 3
        - name: "user_activity_events"
          partitions: 24
          retention: "7_days"
  
  # Infrastructure Layer
  infrastructure:
    container_orchestration:
      platform: "kubernetes"
      cluster_configuration:
        master_nodes: 3
        worker_nodes: 12
        auto_scaling: "horizontal_pod_autoscaler"
    
    monitoring_observability:
      metrics: "prometheus_grafana"
      logging: "elk_stack"
      tracing: "jaeger_distributed_tracing"
      alerting: "alertmanager_pagerduty"
    
    security:
      identity_management: "okta_enterprise"
      secret_management: "hashicorp_vault"
      network_security: "zero_trust_architecture"
      data_encryption: "aes_256_at_rest_tls_in_transit"
  
  # Cross-Cutting Concerns
  quality_attributes:
    scalability:
      horizontal_scaling: "auto_scaling_based_on_metrics"
      vertical_scaling: "resource_optimization"
      capacity_planning: "predictive_analytics"
    
    availability:
      target_sla: "99.99%"
      disaster_recovery: "rpo_1h_rto_4h"
      health_checks: "comprehensive_multi_layer"
    
    performance:
      response_time_target: "sub_2_second_p95"
      throughput_target: "10000_concurrent_users"
      optimization: "continuous_profiling"
    
    security:
      compliance: ["sox", "gdpr", "hipaa"]
      penetration_testing: "quarterly"
      vulnerability_scanning: "continuous"
Multi-tier enterprise architecture provides clear separation of concerns while enabling independent scaling and evolution of different system layers.

Modern enterprise architectures require sophisticated integration patterns that enable loose coupling, fault tolerance, and scalable communication between PEGA applications and external systems. Advanced patterns provide resilient, maintainable integration solutions.

Architectural governance ensures consistency, quality, and alignment with enterprise standards across all PEGA implementations. Advanced governance frameworks provide automated compliance checking, design review processes, and continuous architectural assessment.

hands_on_exercises.title: Enterprise Architecture Design Implementation
hands_on_exercises.description: Design and implement a complete enterprise PEGA architecture with advanced patterns and governance
steps: Design multi-tier enterprise architecture with scalability and resilience patterns
Implement microservices integration patterns with event-driven architecture
Configure architectural governance framework with automated compliance checking
Create comprehensive architecture documentation and standards compliance report
Validate architecture through performance testing and scalability assessment

best_practices: Use proven architectural patterns to ensure scalability and maintainability
Implement comprehensive governance processes with automated compliance checking
Design for failure with circuit breakers, bulkheads, and graceful degradation
Establish clear separation of concerns through well-defined architectural layers
Maintain architectural documentation and standards alignment through continuous assessment
common_pitfalls: Over-engineering solutions without considering business complexity requirements
Insufficient architectural governance leading to inconsistent implementations
Poor integration patterns causing tight coupling and scalability issues
Inadequate consideration of non-functional requirements in architectural design
